description.text: The track levels out onto open heather. The flock is a pale smudge folded against the drystone wall, and two cottages sit further along the slope — one with a shuttered light, one dark. Above them the ground rises to a black tree line that the moonlight does not get into.

The track levels out onto open heather, all gorse and bee-hum and sheep-cropped turf. Orik's flock works its way along a drystone wall; past them stand the shepherd's cot and, further along the slope, the beekeeper's cottage with its row of hives. The tree line above is close enough to see individual trunks.

options.text: Talk to Lira on her way up to the hives
Go back down to the crossroads

skills.text: Look up at the tree line
resultText: Where the heather gives out, the grass is flattened in a long band going uphill — wide as a dragged ewe, and it stops dead about forty feet short of the trees. Nothing enters the wood. Nothing leaves it.

You find the end of the flattened band again and crouch at it. No prints, no dew-break, no broken gorse. The grass simply gives up being flattened, as though whatever made the track was set down here and lifted away.
One of Orik's dogs comes and sits at your knee facing the trees, and does not look away from them, and does not make a sound.
